headline: Tentative relief after Friday’s semiconductor shock—not a confirmed momentum recovery. Recorded premarket snapshots only; AMD’s forecast was published after the open.
market_bullets: Coverage 10/10 same-day notes: 7 Today calls flat-to-up versus 3 flat-to-down. No pure-up Today calls; directional confidence remains modest.
All ten latest recorded RSI readings are below 50; 5/10 VEL5 readings are negative. Positive five-bar readings in MU, ARM, ASML, SIMO and AMD still coexist with sharp latest-bar damage.

Nine recorded indications are green; Intel remains red after a 28.58% Friday collapse. These asynchronous snapshots imply tentative sector relief plus Intel-specific weakness, not an all-clear or live breadth measurement.
Earnings cluster is the next test: AMD November 3; ARM and Qualcomm November 4; Cloudflare November 5. NVIDIA follows November 17, and TSMC monthly sales November 10, per the source notes.
Funding is not demand: Oracle’s proposed debt/equity and hyperscaler financing can support capacity, but neither proves settled cash, accepted GPU systems or incremental supplier orders.
SIMO and MU lead the low-conviction rebound ranking; cash conversion, labor/production and competitive supply still matter. Qualcomm’s HBC engineering milestone does not establish paid production.

Monthly calibration remains weak across several notes; do not mistake broad band hits for directional skill. Preserve each note’s target/maturity conventions; AMD’s after-open publication is not a strictly frozen premarket forecast.

All prices are archived November 2 premarket indications and technicals reflect October 30 completed bars. No quotes or ticker research were refreshed; ranges are terminal-close scenarios, not actionable intraday limits.
